info.title: Harness Control API
info.description: Local management API of Harness Studio (llama.cpp control center). Every endpoint except /health needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: the session token (`<data dir>/api-token`, full access) or a named token with scopes (read, inference, models:write, downloads:write, servers:write, servers:control, conversations, admin); a token's gateway policy (allowed models and endpoints, rate limits) is part of it. Errors: `{"error": {"code", "message_key", "params"}}`.

the gateway (`harness serve --gateway` or the app's gateway), so it queues like any other
request. One compaction per conversation at a time (409 `compaction.busy`).

exposure_acknowledged.description: Started on a network address without an API key after the user's "open anyway".

cors_origins.description: `--cors-origins` sent to this run (`None` = llama-server's default).

serve_mode.description: What this run serves: chat, embeddings (`--embeddings`) or reranking (`--rerank`).

engine_family.description:
Runtime family serving this run (`llama.cpp`, `mlx`, `mlx-vlm`, `mlx-audio`, ...): the
routes a client can call depend on it. Empty for runs recorded before it existed.

AdapterRef.description: A LoRA adapter applied at load.

copy.description: Copy the folder's top-level files under the data dir instead of using it in place.

family.description: Runtime family of the folder (default llama.cpp).

AddRuntimeRequest.description: Add request: a GitHub release (`github`) or a local folder (`local`).

totals.description:
Gateway statistics (`alias` = `*`); requests also include attributed direct clients.
Timings and error rates only cover gateway requests with recorded outcomes.

models.description: Per gateway model, most requests first.

raw_since_ms.description: Oldest raw row still stored; percentiles only cover raw rows.

rollup_days.description: Days in the range that only survive as daily rollups (older than the raw retention).

direct.description:
Token totals of the llama-server ports that bypass the gateway (aggregate only; see
`analytics::direct`).

AutomaticLaunch.description:
Everything an automatic default load starts with, for forms and `harness show` that display it
before Start: the full-offload choice plus the slot count and the KV cache the launch ends
up with (the cache types and the flash attention they need).

slots.description: Concurrent requests (`-np`) the launch runs with; `None` when no slot plan applies.

cache_type_k.description: Cache types of the automatic KV precision (`f16` for the full level).

flash_attn.description: A quantized V cache needs flash attention: the launch turns it on.

additionalProperties.description: A catalog value. Untagged so presets stay plain JSON (`{"jinja": true, "cache_ram": 4096}`).

BackendAdvice.description: Why a backend is recommended, for the UI (`reason_key` is an i18n key under `backend.`).

alternatives.description: Other official builds that also run on this GPU.

BackendInfo.description: A backend Lemonade can run models on, from `GET /v1/system-info` `recipes`.

version.description: Release tag Lemonade pins for this backend (`b10825`).

message.description: Why it is not usable on this machine (`Unsupported GPU`).

BenchResult.description: One llama-bench result row (a subset of its JSON output).

flash_attn.description: -1 auto / 0 off / 1 on (older builds report a bool).

current.description: The current (or latest) run's live state.

BenchmarkRef.description: A benchmark result next to real usage.

prompt_tps.description: Best prompt-processing result (`pp` test) of the run, t/s.

gen_tps.description: Best generation result (`tg` test) of the run, t/s.

n_prompt.description: Each list is a sweep: llama-bench runs every combination.

concurrent_servers.description:
Servers that held GPU memory when the run started (set by the front end that knows the
registry, not by the caller): their load skews the numbers, so the saved run keeps it.

run_id.description: Id of the current (or latest) run; the saved run gets the same id.

oneOf.description: Set when the latest run finished (saved to history).

oneOf.description: Live state (the current run only).

BinarySource.description: Where the official runtime's binary comes from.

and the card show the choices without starting a server.

updated_at.description: Unix seconds of the refresh (0 = never).

requires_token.description: Requests need a token (managed: gateway setting; direct: the server has an API key).

token_name.description: Name of the named token used (`harness` for the gateway's own client token).

label.description:

share.description: Share of all requests in the range (0–1).

keep_turns.description: Newest turns kept as they are (default 2; fewer when they exceed 40 % of the context).

clear_tool_results.description: Shorten old tool results before summarizing (default true).

summary_tokens.description: Summary budget in tokens (default 1/8 of the context, 256 to 2048).

instruction.description: Extra instruction for the summary ("keep the numbers").

marker_id.description: Id of the marker message (undo it with `PUT .../compactions/{marker_id}`).

marker.description: What was compacted: the token counts before and after, the turns kept.

CompactionMarker.description: The compaction marker stored in `meta.compaction` of the marker message's variant.

boundary_id.description: Last message the summary covers; the request continues after it.

covered.description: Conversation messages the summary covers (including what an earlier summary covered).

kept_turns.description: Turns kept verbatim after the boundary when it was made.

tokens_before.description: Prompt tokens of the conversation before / after (system, summary, kept turns).

exact_tokens.description: Token counts came from the server's tokenizer (else estimated).

previous_id.description: Earlier marker whose summary was folded into this one.

undone.description: Undone by the user: the request ignores it (and auto-compaction pauses on this path).

mid_turn.description: Made while an answer was still running (between two tool rounds), see [`plan_mid_turn`].

pinned_id.description:
The user message of the running turn: it lies before the boundary but is still sent
verbatim right after the summary (a request must keep the question it answers).

CompactionSettings.description:
Context compaction of stored Responses chains (`gateway.responses.compaction`; see
ARCHITECTURE §9.1): when the conversation a `previous_response_id` continues no longer fits
the model comfortably, its older links are replaced, in the request, by a summary the model
writes. The summary is stored on the new response (`harness_compaction`), so later turns
start from it instead of the whole chain. Always opt-in: a request asks for it with
`context_management: [{"type": "compaction", "compact_threshold": <tokens>}]`, or the
setting turns it on for every chained request.

auto.description: Compact every chained request that crosses the threshold, not only the ones that ask.

threshold_percent.description:
Share of the model's context window (per slot) the conversation may fill before it is
compacted.

keep_links.description: Newest links kept as they are (their input and output); older ones are summarized.

oneOf.description: An installed (or always available) runtime family runs it.
The family that runs it is not installed yet.

The family that runs it has no build for this OS / architecture (ONNX Runtime on an
Intel Mac): nothing to install, the model cannot run here.
No Harness runtime runs this format.

Compatibility.description: Whether Harness can run a repo.

settings.description: Sampling snapshot (opaque JSON object owned by the client).

documents.description:
Documents attached for local RAG (`ready` ones, with their text and chunks). Absent in
files written before documents were exported.

ConversationSummary.description: One row of the conversation list.

snippet.description: Matching text fragment when the list comes from a search.

ConvertJob.description: One conversion, as the queue shows it.

keep_original.description: The downloaded safetensors are kept in the library after the conversion.

progress.description: Fraction of the current stage, `None` when it has no measure.

detail.description: The file or line the stage is on (technical text, not translated).

error.description: Keyed error of a failed job.

mmproj.description: The finished vision projector, when the model has one.

warning.description: Keyed note that does not fail the job (`convert.mmproj_failed`).

kept_bytes.description: Size of the partial files a failed or cancelled job left for a retry.

reason.description: Why it does not: a keyed error (`convert.unsupported_architecture`...).

vision.description: The converter also writes a vision projector for it (image-text-to-text).

parameters.description: Parameter count (from the Hub's safetensors header summary, else estimated).

embedding_parameters.description:
Parameters of the token embedding (`vocab_size * hidden_size` of the config; 0 unknown):
kept at a higher precision than the rest, so a small model's file is bigger than its
parameter count says.

fallback_parameters.description:
Weights of matrices whose rows are not a multiple of 256 (0 unknown or none): a k-quant
target cannot hold them, so `llama-quantize` stores them in a wider fallback type.

free_bytes.description: Free bytes on the drive of the model library.

env_ready.description: The conversion environment matches the runtime and is ready.

env_estimated_bytes.description: Rough size a first build of the environment adds (0 when it is ready).

runtime_tag.description: llama.cpp tag of the managed runtime the GGUF is made for.

architectures_checked.description: The architecture list of the converter was available (false: only the task was checked).

base_model.description:
The model this one was made from (`base_model` of the card): for a checkpoint the
converter cannot read, a GGUF of the base model is the way to run it.

repo.description: Hugging Face repo (`owner/name`) with safetensors weights.

quant.description:
Target type (`Q4_K_M` default, `Q5_K_M`, `Q6_K`, `Q8_0`, `F16`, `BF16`, or any type
the runtime's `llama-quantize` lists).

keep_original.description: Keep the downloaded safetensors in the library after the conversion.

chat_template_text.description:

DirectServer.description: Tokens of one server run in a range.

Direct usage in the range of an analytics summary: aggregate token totals only, no
per-request detail. See the module docs for how it is derived.

AMD GPU usable by the official ROCm/HIP build: Windows with an AMD GPU (the release
archive bundles the HIP runtime), Linux with the amdgpu KFD node (`/dev/kfd`).

EffectiveLaunchValues.description: What the server actually runs with, next to what was requested.

gpu_layers_source.description:
Where the GPU layer count comes from: `log` (the `offloaded N/M` line, printed only
at `-lv 4` / `--verbose`) or `derived` (llama.cpp's rule applied to `-ngl`, the
model's `block_count` and the runtime's GPU devices). `None` when unknown.

ctx_adjusted.description: The server picked a different context than requested (`-c 0` or `--fit`).

kv_fa_fallback.description: K/V pair the CUDA build converts to f16 on every token (slow), see [`kv_fa_fallback`].

fit_failed.description:
llama-server could not fit the settings into free device memory and started anyway
([`fit_params_failed`]): on Windows the driver may spill the excess into shared system
memory.

shared_memory_slowdown.description: Smaller shared-memory pressure, separate from failure to fit.

What the running server actually uses (`None` until checked after start).

estimated_size_bytes.description: Rough size a first build adds.

oneOf.description: Progress of the build running now.

code.description:
Stable machine code (`api.unauthorized`, `network.lan_without_key`, `fs.read_failed`...).
`core.error` only for the rare core errors that are free text.

message_key.description: i18n key of the message (Harness Studio locale files; same as `code`).

params.description:
Values for the message's `{name}` placeholders (`path`, `error`, `detail`, `message`,
`scope`...). Technical detail (paths, OS error text) is untranslated; a string value may
itself be a keyed error (`key {"name": "value"}` or `key: detail`), a nested cause.

ExportedDocument.description:
A document of the conversation. A file export carries the text and chunks but no vectors:
an imported document is searchable by keywords at once and gets embeddings again when the
user indexes it with an embedding model. Duplicating or forking a conversation copies the
vectors as well (the `embedding` fields never reach a file).

meta.description: Client metadata (split-view side...). Absent in files written before schema v4.

host.description: The network address the server binds (as shown to the user).

FailureKind.description: Failure classes, most specific first (the order [`classify`] tries them).

FileDigest.description: One hashed file of a runtime.

measured_at.description: Unix ms of the measurement used (`source` corrected/measured).

recommended_gpu_layers.description: The `-ngl` that keeps the estimate under 90% of the budget (layer count + 1 = full).

oneOf.description:
Concurrent requests (slots): the automatic choice or the set value and the
recommendation ([`fit`] only).
The automatic KV precision the estimate used (`kv_auto` inputs only).

canonical.description: First long (`--x`) spelling that is not a `--no-` negation; else the first spelling.

aliases.description: Every spelling on the header line (including `canonical` and negations), in order.

enum_values.description: Allowed values when the help lists them (hint, "allowed values:" or a `- x:` list).

description.description: Description with continuation lines joined by single spaces.

removed.description: Still listed but "the argument has been removed"; never emitted.

ForkHint.description: A fork that adds tensor types of its own.

repo.description: GitHub `owner/repo` that publishes the release archives.

GatewayEndpoint.description: Gateway route groups a token can be limited to.

GatewaySettings.description:
`settings.json` → `gateway`. Changed only through [`validate_settings`] (the general
settings save keeps the stored block, like `control_api`).

enabled.description:
Off by default; the user turns it on (Settings > Gateway) or runs `harness serve
--gateway`.

allow_network.description: A non-loopback bind must be allowed explicitly and always requires a token.

require_token.description:
Require a token on loopback too (a network bind always does). Accepted: named tokens
with the `inference` (or `admin`) scope, and the gateway's own client token.

cors_origins.description: Browser origins allowed by CORS (the Harness window is always allowed).

max_loaded_models.description: Models the gateway keeps loaded at once (0 = no limit; memory decides).

max_queue.description:
Requests that may wait per definition (for a load or a free slot); more → 503 +
`Retry-After`.

request_timeout_secs.description:
Seconds a request may wait for a slot and for the upstream response to start, and the
longest pause inside a stream. 0 = no limit.

default_ttl_secs.description:
Idle unload after this many seconds for definitions without their own TTL. `None`
(default) = never.

memory_aware.description:
Evict least recently used idle models when the next one does not fit in free VRAM
(estimate/measurement of `vram.rs`, free memory of `--list-devices`).

memory_headroom_mib.description:
VRAM kept free on top of the estimate, MiB. 0 = automatic (`vram::memory_headroom`:
max(1 GiB, 8% of the card)); a value above 0 is used as given. A stored 512 (the old
default) loads as 0.

tool_ignores.description:
Explicit per-definition consent to ignore tools the local server cannot run
(definition id → tool types or names, e.g. `web_search`). Every ignored tool is
reported in the `X-Harness-Compat` response header and in the log.

server_tools.description:
Server-side tools, per definition id: the gateway runs the tool loop itself for
these models instead of rejecting hosted tools. Off (empty) by default; see
[`ServerTools`].

text_tool_calls.description:
Recover calls left in Chat Completions text, per definition. On by default: only an
explicit `false` (the opt-out) is stored; a definition without an entry recovers. A
request that offers no tools is never touched.

ollama_port_enabled.description:
Also listen on the Ollama port (`ollama_port`, default 11434) with the same routes, for
clients that only know Ollama's address. Off by default. When something already
answers there (a real Ollama), the gateway does not bind it and reports
`GatewayStatus::ollama_warning` instead; Ollama's default port is also refused while
Ollama is installed (not running), so a later Ollama start still works.

ollama_allow_pull.description:
Let `/api/pull` queue Hugging Face downloads (explicit `hf.co/<owner>/<repo>[:quant]`
references only). Off by default.

oneOf.description:
Stateful `/v1/responses` (`store`, `previous_response_id`): on by default, stored in
`state.db` with retention (see [`responses`]).

decision_emulation.description:
`/v1/systemone` and `/v1/decisions` with a chat model: the gateway asks the model one
constrained question per decision (GBNF grammar) and reads the probabilities from its
logprobs. On by default; off = only native decision models answer, as in Ollama and LM
Studio.

GatewayStatus.description: What the gateway listener is doing right now (process-wide; set by the HTTP side).

oneOf.description: The managed endpoint while running.

error.description: Why the last start failed (i18n key or text).

ollama_port.description: The Ollama port the gateway also listens on (`ollama_port_enabled`), when bound.

ollama_warning.description: Why the Ollama port is not served (i18n key `WARN_OLLAMA_*`, `: <port>` appended).

oneOf.description:
The configured port was held by another program: the gateway runs on `port` instead
(remembered in `config/ports.json`; Harness's client configs follow it).

clients_moved.description: Client configs Harness moved to this port at the start (display names).

clients_pending.description:
Client configs still on another address after that (a key in the file, a server's own
port): their card shows the warning with "Düzelt".

models.description: Definitions the scheduler knows (loaded, loading or used since the gateway started).

audiocpp_family.description: audio.cpp model family; only meaningful for architecture = audiocpp.

url.description:
Provenance URLs that may identify a Hugging Face repository when a split file was
copied into the library by hand.

sliding_window_pattern.description:
`<arch>.attention.sliding_window_pattern` as a number: every N-th layer is a full
attention layer, the others use the window (llama.cpp `set_swa_pattern(N)`).

swa_layer_count.description:
`<arch>.attention.sliding_window_pattern` as a per-layer array: number of layers that
use the window.

key_length_swa.description:
`<arch>.attention.key_length_swa` / `value_length_swa`: head size of the
sliding-window layers when it differs from the full-attention layers (Gemma 4).

head_count_kv_swa.description:
KV heads of the sliding-window and of the full-attention layers, from the per-layer
`head_count_kv` and `sliding_window_pattern` arrays (Gemma 4: 8 and 1). `None` when
the file has no per-layer arrays (then `head_count_kv` applies to every layer).

attention_layer_count.description:
Layers with attention (a KV cache) of hybrid models whose per-layer `head_count_kv`
array is 0 for the recurrent layers (Jamba, Granite hybrid, Nemotron-H).

full_attention_interval.description:
`<arch>.full_attention_interval`: every N-th layer has attention, the others are
recurrent (Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5/3.6).

ssm_conv_kernel.description:
`<arch>.ssm.*` of recurrent / hybrid models (Mamba, gated delta net): they keep one
fixed-size state per sequence (= per server slot).

rope_scaling_original_ctx.description:
`<arch>.rope.scaling.original_context_length`: context the model was trained on before
the scaling.

token_embd_bytes.description: Bytes of `token_embd.weight` (llama.cpp keeps it in host memory for the lookup).

output_bytes.description:
Bytes of `output.weight`; `None` with `token_embd_bytes` set = tied output (llama.cpp
then also uploads a copy of the embeddings as the output layer).

template_supports_tools.description: The embedded chat template handles `tools` (native tool/function calling).

pooling_type.description: Tokenizer / pooling hints for embedding & reranker models.

is_mmproj.description: True for multimodal projector files (`general.type = mmproj` / clip architecture).

has_classifier_labels.description: A `<arch>.classifier.output_labels` key exists (classification heads, e.g. rerankers).

decision_type.description:
`<arch>.decision.type` (`vllm-d3`, `decision2`...): a native decision model, served
through llama-server's `/v1/systemone` (llama.cpp lists it with the `decisions` output
modality).

has_cls_head.description:
A sequence-classification head (`cls.output.weight` / `cls.weight` tensors), which is
how BERT/XLM-R rerankers such as bge-reranker-v2-m3 are stored (no `pooling_type` key).

basename.description: `general.basename` (pairs a projector with its model: both carry the same basename).

param_count.description:
Sum of the element counts of the tensors described in this file (exact; for split
models only this shard's tensors). `None` when the tensor table could not be read.

split_count.description: `split.count` of split GGUFs (0 or absent for single files).

template_supports_reasoning.description:
The embedded chat template can switch reasoning on (`enable_thinking`,
`reasoning_effort`, gpt-oss channels, or an unconditional `<think>` opener).

oneOf.description: Tokenizer facts used to match draft models with their target.

tensor_types.description:
Distinct ggml tensor types of this file (numeric `ggml_type` ids, sorted). Used to tell
whether a runtime can load the file (fork-only quant types; see `runtimes::quant`).

legacy_prism_q2_0.description:
Type 42 whose byte spans match Prism's deprecated group-128 layout rather than
upstream Q2_0's group-64 layout. Only set when the tensor table proves the difference.

allow_unverified.description: The user saw the archive name, size and URL and accepts that it has no digest.

GpuMemory.description: VRAM of one graphics adapter (a machine with several: discrete card plus integrated GPU).

oneOf.description: Used VRAM of this adapter by consumer; None where the OS has no per-process counter.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file as published by Hugging Face (LFS oid), when known.

builtin.description: Shipped with the app; read-only (copy it to change it).

SHA-256 the download was checked against (`None` = none published; installed only
after the user confirmed).

InstalledFile.description: One file of an installed build.

InstanceKind.description: Which program owns the data directory.

Unload after this many idle seconds (`0` = as soon as the last request ends).

secs.description: Unload after this many idle seconds (`0` = as soon as the last request ends).

KeepAlive.description:
Ollama `keep_alive` of the last Ollama-API request for a definition (overrides the idle
TTL of a gateway-loaded model; pinned definitions are never unloaded).

kv_bytes_f16.description: Whole KV cache with f16 and with this choice (bytes).

prompt_slowdown_pct.description:
Typical prompt-processing slowdown of this choice vs f16 on the machine's backend
(percent, measured; `None` = not measured for this backend).

KvReason.description: Why the automatic choice is what it is.

LastRequest.description: Work done by the request(s) that finished between two samples.

prompt_seconds.description: Time spent on the prompt: the closest thing to time-to-first-token /metrics offers.

port.description: The listening port. With `port_auto` (or 0) it is only the last automatic pick.

port_auto.description:
Harness picks the port (`ports::AUTO_RANGE`, 11440–11499): `port` is kept while it is
free, else another one is taken silently. Off = the user chose `port`; a taken port is
then an error naming the program that holds it. Port 0 means the same as on.

main_gpu.description:
Main GPU as an OS adapter index (`gpu::GpuAdapter::index`, what the GPU picker shows),
not the runtime's device index; converted at launch (`devices::pair_adapters`).

api_key_ref.description: Keychain reference of the saved key (safe to store and to send to the UI).

mcp_config_path.description: Resolved by the backend at launch (never trusted from the frontend).

params.description:
Catalog parameters (`params.toml`) without a typed field above; emitted only when
the runtime has the flag.

runtime.description:
Runtime (llama-server build) of this launch: a `runtimes` registry id; `None` or
`official` = Settings > Runtime. Resolved to `binary_path` by the orchestrator.

alias.description: Served model id (`--alias`): the ModelDefinition's alias. `None` = the file stem.

definition_id.description:
The ModelDefinition this launch was resolved from (informational: lets the UI and the
Dashboard session know which definition a server runs).

launched_by.description:
Who starts the server: the gateway's JIT loads serve agents, which decides the
automatic slot count (`slots`). Set by the backend.

auto_fields.description:
Settings (catalog ids) that hold the automatic choice, not a value anyone set: the
context, layer count and slot count a form shows from the default-load rule
(`full_offload`), and the layer count of a resolved definition launch. They are left
out of every layer made from this config (`domain::launch::config_layer`), so a
profile, definition or last session never freezes them as explicit values.

size_gb.description: Download size in GB, as Lemonade lists it.

LemonadeSettings.description: Harness's settings of the Lemonade engine (`<data>/lemonade/settings.json`).

runtime.description:
Registry id of the Lemonade build to run (`None` = the newest installed one). Pinning
an older one is the rollback.

supported.description: Lemonade publishes a build for this OS and CPU.

running_runtime.description: Registry id of the build that is running.

npu.description: An AMD Ryzen AI NPU is present (FastFlowLM / Ryzen AI backends need one).

backends.description: Backends as of the last run.

install_progress.description: Progress of the running release download.

oneOf.description: Progress of the running model pull / backend install.

LibraryEntry.description: One local model file (or split set) as the library shows it.

record.description:
Capabilities, format and runtime of the file as the model registry joins them
([`crate::model_registry`]); the same record the Hub builds for a repo.

pairs.description: LLM: projector files that belong to it. Projector: the LLMs it belongs to (ids).

multimodal.description: LLM with a projector (or vision in a definition): "VLM / multimodal".

Incomplete split models only.

repo_id.description:
Hugging Face repo (`owner/name`) the file was downloaded from, read from its folder
(`<library>/<owner>/<repo>/…`); the UI shows the owner's avatar.

preset_used.description:
Preset used last: the newest conversation with one of its aliases, else the default
preset of the definition that started it last.

added_at.description: When the file arrived (Unix ms; download completion or copy time).

draft_for.description: Bigger local LLMs this one can draft for (ids).

LoadAdaptation.description:
Cache types and context the gateway loaded a model with to fit it into the free memory

Layers left on the GPU when even the smallest context did not fit the whole model

scale.description: Current scale (0 = loaded but not applied).

McpServerStatus.description: What `mcp-client status` shows for one configured server.

server.description: `serverInfo` as the server reports it (display only).

oneOf.description: OAuth state of an HTTP server (`None` for stdio servers and servers that never asked).

MemoryBreakdown.description:
Used memory (system RAM or VRAM) split into Harness Studio, its llama-server processes
and everything else. Process figures are working sets (RAM) or dedicated GPU memory
(VRAM); shared RAM pages can be counted in more than one process, so `other_bytes`
saturates at 0 instead of going negative.

harness_bytes.description: This app's process and its child processes (the WebView2 ones on Windows).

vram_bytes.description: Device memory for offload (0 = CPU only).

unified.description: Apple Silicon: `vram_bytes` is the GPU share of unified memory.

shared_igpu.description:
Integrated GPU without dedicated memory (Intel HD/UHD/Iris, AMD APU): `vram_bytes` is
the part of system RAM the driver lets it use, the same pool as `ram_bytes`.

igpu_offload_faster.description:
Integrated GPU: whether offloading the weights generates faster than keeping them on
the CPU. From a llama-bench run of this model with both `-ngl 0` and a full offload
(Performance > Benchmark); otherwise from the device class (older Intel HD/UHD/Iris:
no). `None`: unknown, the memory budget decides.

cuda.description:
The machine's backend is CUDA: its default build has no flash-attention kernel for
mixed K/V cache types (see [`crate::kv_policy`]).

rocm.description: ROCm/HIP: matching K/V pairs avoid the measured slow generation path.

MemoryEstimate.description: Where the memory goes, in bytes.

compute_host_bytes.description: Compute buffer in host memory (CPU-only runs).

output_host_bytes.description: llama.cpp's host-visible logits output buffer (one row per physical batch token).

kv_cells.description: KV cells of the full-attention layers (padded context).

swa_layers.description: Layers with sliding-window attention and their (smaller) cache size.

recurrent_bytes.description: Recurrent state of all sequences (part of `kv_bytes`; Mamba / gated delta net layers).

checkpoint_bytes.description:
Context checkpoints at most (host memory, part of `ram_bytes`): slots x
`--ctx-checkpoints` x one window / state copy. 0 for models without SWA / recurrent
layers (they need none).

exact.description: Layer count and KV shape came from the GGUF header (else a size-based guess).

draft_gpu_bytes.description: Draft model (weights + its KV cache + compute) in device memory, part of `vram_bytes`.

draft_host_bytes.description: Draft model in host memory, part of `ram_bytes`.

MessageAttachment.description: Attachment metadata (the file itself is not part of the database or the export).

ModelCaps.description: What a model can do, from its header, template and companion files.

vision.description: A vision projector belongs to it (matched file, linked projector or a definition).

audio.description: Its projector has an audio encoder.

audio_input.description: Audio content parts accepted by the model, independent of vision.

asr.description: Speech recognition (Whisper, sherpa-onnx or an ONNX CTC package).

tts.description: Speech synthesis (a Kokoro or Piper folder run by sherpa-onnx).

oneOf.description:
What `/props` of a real run of this file reported; `None` until it was loaded once.
Without it `tools` / `reasoning` come from the chat template text.

ModelDefinition.description: A logical model: what clients ask for by `alias`.

chat_template.description: Built-in template name or template file (`--chat-template`).

extra_args.description: Extra command-line arguments (same rules as the Dashboard's custom args field).

load.description:
Default load settings: catalog ids (`params.toml`) -> value. The typed fields above are
never duplicated here.

ttl_seconds.description: Reserved for the gateway (idle unload after N seconds).

capture_content.description:
Store the request and response content of gateway requests to this definition in
`analytics.db`. Off by default: only metadata is recorded.

auto_created.description:
Created by Harness Studio itself (v2 migration, a profile saved without a definition,
the Dashboard session). Deleted again when the profile that owned it goes away and
nothing else references it. Cleared as soon as the user edits the definition.

ModelFormat.description: The format a repo's model files are in.

ModelKind.description: What a GGUF file is. Decided from its header by [`detect_kind`].

live.description: `lemond` is running (the list is current); otherwise it is the last snapshot.

ModelList.description: The registry as the card shows it.

ModelRecord.description: Capability, format and runtime verdict of one model (a local file or a Hub repo).

runtime.description: Runtime family that runs the format (`None`: no Harness runtime does).

oneOf.description: `None` for a file that is not served on its own (projector, adapter, unreadable).
A local GGUF (`LocalModel.id`: canonical launch path; shard 1 for split models).
A Hugging Face file not downloaded yet (`hf:<repo>:<file>`).

model.description: A Lemonade registry name (`Qwen3-0.6B-GGUF`) or a checkpoint (`owner/repo[:variant]`).

ModelSlot.description: One definition as the gateway sees it (GUI table, Control API `/gateway`).

managed.description:
Loaded by the gateway (counts against the limits, may be evicted / unloaded by TTL).
`false` = a server the user started; the gateway only routes to it.

ttl_secs.description:
Effective idle TTL (Ollama `keep_alive` override, else the definition's, else the
gateway default).

oneOf.description: `keep_alive` of the last Ollama-API request, while it overrides the TTL.

concurrency.description: Requests that may run at once (llama-server slots).

waited.description:
Requests that had to wait for a free slot since the model was loaded (all slots were
busy): a hint to give the model more concurrent requests at its next load.

token_pool.description:
Token budget of the shared KV pool (`-c` with `--kv-unified` and several slots; 0 = no
budget) and the part the running requests hold (their estimates).

waited_tokens.description:
Requests that had a free slot but waited for room in the shared KV pool since the model
was loaded (more slots do not help these; a larger context does).

idle_secs.description: Seconds since the last request finished.

oneOf.description:
The current load was fitted into the free memory with other cache types / context than
the definition's.

ModelStats.description: Statistics of one model (alias) over a time range.

alias.description: Alias (`*` for the total row; empty for requests that never resolved a model).

avg_gen_tps.description: Generated tokens / generation time over every timed request (token-weighted).

ttft_p50_ms.description: Percentiles come from raw rows only (the last `retention_days`).

percentile_samples.description: Raw rows the latency percentiles are computed from.

vram_avg_bytes.description: Mean of the per-request VRAM peaks.

busy_ms.description: Sum of request durations (time the model was busy for clients).

oneOf.description: Latest completed llama-bench run of the definition's model file.

ModelfileImport.description: What a Modelfile import found (nothing is saved yet).

warnings.description: What could not be carried over.

ModelfileMapped.description: One value the import sets, for the preview.

ModelfileRequest.description: Request of the Control API / GUI: a Modelfile's text and where its relative paths start.

ModelfileWarning.description:
Something that could not be carried over. `code` is stable (the UI translates it);
`detail` is the instruction / parameter / value concerned.

ModelsResponse.description:
The library: every local model (all kinds: LLM, embedding, reranker, projector, adapter)
plus the model definitions built on them.

detected.description: An AMD XDNA NPU is present.

name.description: Device name as the OS reports it.

driver_installed.description:
The driver is installed (Windows: the device is named "NPU Compute Accelerator Device"
/ class `ComputeAccelerator`; Linux: the `amdxdna` module is bound). Without it the
NPU exists but no backend can use it.

OfficialState.description: The honest state of the official runtime (Settings > Runtime).

oneOf.description: Where the binary used now comes from (`None` = nothing found).

fallback.description:
The configured mode can't be honored (e.g. managed build not installed), so the binary
used is a fallback (a system llama-server found on PATH / WinGet...).

managed_version.description: Version the settings record for the managed build.

oneOf.description: A downloaded managed build that passed stage 1 but was never activated.

problems.description: Files whose hash differs or that are missing.

OtelProtocol.description: Wire protocol of the OTLP endpoint.

OtelSettings.description:
`settings.json` → `otel`. Changed only through [`save_settings`] (the general settings
save keeps the stored block, like `gateway` and `control_api`).

endpoint.description:
Collector base URL (`http://host:4318` for HTTP, `http://host:4317` for gRPC). For HTTP
the signal paths `/v1/traces`, `/v1/logs` and `/v1/metrics` are appended.

logs.description: Gateway request log records. Off by default, independently of traces.

include_content.description: Put prompts and answers on spans, only for model definitions that capture content.

header_names.description: Names of the extra export headers; the values live in the OS keychain.

OtelStatus.description: Exporter state for Settings and diagnostics.

built.description: This build contains the exporter (cargo feature `otel`).

grpc.description:
This build can export over OTLP/gRPC (cargo feature `otel-grpc`); OTLP/HTTP is always
there when `built`.

spans_dropped.description: Spans dropped because the export queue was full.

last_export_ms.description: Unix ms of the last successful span export.

PathMessage.description: A message on the current path, with its shown variant and navigation info.

variant_ids.description: All variants of this message, oldest first.

sibling_ids.description: Messages sharing this message's parent (and parent variant), oldest first.

compare.description:
Split view: every variant of the shown variant's comparison group (sides `a`, `b`),
in side order. Empty when the shown variant is not part of a comparison.

compare_groups.description:
Split view: one variant id per comparison group of this message (the side-`a` variant),
oldest group first. More than one group means the turn was regenerated; the shown
group is the one `compare` belongs to. Empty when the message has no comparison.

PermissionClass.description:
What a tool may do to the user's machine. The class is fixed by the tool's author (the
registry entry), never by the model or by call arguments: nothing a model sends can make a
tool less restricted than it was registered.

Phase.description: One segment of a request's timeline, in ms from its arrival at the gateway.

kind.description:
`load` (JIT load of the model), `queue` (waiting for a free slot), `prompt` (prompt
processing), `generation` (token generation), `other` (proxy, network, sampling
overhead after the model's own timings).

PlanFile.description: One file of the repo that is downloaded.

sha256.description: SHA-256 Hugging Face publishes for the file (LFS), checked after the download.

PlatformSupport.description: [`supported`] with the OS and architecture it was decided for (the UI names them).

PortFallback.description: A listener that could not use its configured port.

configured.description: The configured port, held by another program.

oneOf.description: That program, when it could be found.

PortHolder.description: The process listening on a port.

name.description: Executable name (`ollama.exe`, `node`...); empty when the process could not be read.

ProfileView.description:
A server profile in the shape the GUI uses (`list_server_profiles` & co.): the effective
launch config of a `domain::ServerProfile` and its `ModelDefinition`.

id.description: Also used as the server instance id when the profile is started.

model_id.description: Model id (= launch path) the profile serves; informational.

description.description: Short free-text purpose ("OpenCode", "Open Design"...); shown in the lists.

auto_start.description: Start this profile when Harness Studio launches.

PullProgress.description: Progress of a model pull or a backend install (the SSE `progress` events of lemond).

target.description: What is being fetched (model name or `recipe:backend`).

total_download_size.description: Size of the whole pull when lemond knows it (0 = unknown).

file.description: A file of the variant (or the variant name). Takes precedence over `quant`.

companions.description:
Download jobs of the companion files a known image model needs (VAE, text encoders);
empty for every other model.

QuantEstimate.description: The result size and disk need of one target type.

disk_bytes.description: Disk the whole run needs at its peak (download + 16-bit GGUF + result).

QueueHint.description:
Queue behaviour of one definition over a time window and, when it keeps making requests
wait for a free slot, how many slots to try at its next load (see
[`AnalyticsDb::queue_hints`]).

slots.description:
Slots of the server at its most recent request in the window; only requests served with
that slot count are counted (an earlier load with other slots says nothing about it).

waited_slots.description: Requests that found every slot busy.

waited_tokens.description:
Requests that had a slot but waited for room in the shared KV pool (more slots would
not help these).

avg_wait_ms.description: Mean queue time of the slot-waiting requests, ms (loads excluded).

suggested_slots.description: Slots worth trying at the next load; `None` while the queue is no problem.

RagDocument.description: A document attached to a conversation (without its text).

tokens.description: Estimated tokens of the whole text (`search::estimate_tokens`).

embedded.description: Chunks that have an embedding of `embed_model`.

error.description: Keyed error of a failed document.

RateLimits.description: Rate limits of one token (`None` = unlimited).

requests_per_minute.description: Requests admitted per minute (token bucket: bursts up to this many, refilled evenly).

tokens_per_minute.description:
Prompt + completion tokens per minute. A request is admitted while the budget is
positive; its tokens are charged when it ends (so one long answer can overdraw it,
and the next request waits until the budget recovers).

max_concurrent.description: Requests of this token in flight at once (streams count until they end).

RecorderStatus.description: Counters of the recorder since this process started.

running.description: The writer thread has started (after the first request).

dropped.description: Dropped because the queue was full.

skipped.description: Skipped because recording is turned off.

overrides.description: Transient layer for the retry (catalog ids).

unload.description: Servers to stop before the retry.

recommended.description: The estimate says this alone should make the model fit.

warning_key.description:
i18n key of a caveat shown with the option (`recovery.ram_insufficient`), its values
are in `params`.

RecoveryPlan.description: The options for a failed server plus what they are based on.

free_vram_bytes.description: Free memory of the target GPU when the plan was made.

estimated_need_bytes.description: Estimated need of the failed launch on the GPU (weights + KV), bytes.

ReleasePick.description: The archive(s) a query resolves to, shown before anything is downloaded.

family.description: Runtime family the archives belong to.

assets.description: Main archive first, then companions (CUDA runtime DLLs).

backend.description: Backend token of the chosen archive (`None` = plain build / explicit asset).

unverified.description: Names of archives without a usable SHA-256 digest (installing needs confirmation).

ReleaseQuery.description: What to install from a repository.

family.description: Runtime family whose release naming picks the archive (default: `llama.cpp`).

tag.description: Release tag (default: the newest release that has a matching archive).

asset.description: Exact archive name (default: picked for this OS/arch and `backend`).

backend.description:
`vulkan`, `cuda`, `rocm`, `sycl`, `cpu`, `metal` (default: the hardware
recommendation, then Vulkan, then CPU).

RemoteResourceTemplate.description: A parameterised resource (`resources/templates/list`, an RFC 6570 URI template).

RepairInfo.description: Where a missing part could come from.

repo_id.description: Hugging Face repo, known from the download layout `<library>/<owner>/<repo>/...`.

reason.description: Why it cannot be repaired automatically (`None` = it can).

source_url.description:
Address of a part that is still there, recorded when the file was downloaded (custom
URL, or a Hugging Face file that no longer sits in its repo folder). The missing parts
are fetched from the same address with the part number replaced.

url_allowed.description:
The user can give the address of one part to repair with (the file is in a library
folder and not linked): offered when there is neither a repo folder nor a record.

timeline.description: load → queue → prompt → generation → other, in ms from arrival.

oneOf.description: Captured content (only for definitions with content capture on, until it expires).

models.description: Values present in the stored rows, for filter pickers.

status.description: HTTP status returned to the client.

cancelled.description: The client went away before the response ended (the upstream request was cancelled).

queue_wait_ms.description: Waiting for a free slot (and for a JIT load), ms.

load_ms.description: JIT load time when this request loaded the model, ms.

evicted.description: Models evicted to make room for this request's load.

ttft_ms.description: First response byte, ms from arrival.

oom.description:
Ran out of memory: no room to load, the load hit OOM, or it did and the retry after
an eviction worked.

ctx_size.description: Context window of one slot of the server that answered (`/props`).

backend.description: ggml backend of that server's build (`vulkan`, `cuda`...).

slots.description: Slots (concurrent requests) of the server that answered.

waited.description:
Why the request waited for its turn: `slots` (all busy) or `tokens` (the shared KV pool
had no room yet); `None` = it ran at once. Feeds the slot recommendation.

tool_involved.description: The request or its response involves tools (offered, called or reported on).

tool_diag_category.description:
Who is at fault when the round went wrong: `runtime`, `context`, `model` or `client`;
`None` for a clean round.

tool_diag_detail.description: Evidence as JSON text (tool name, excerpt, schema path, linked request...).

client.description: Client label (`X-Harness-Client`, token name, `User-Agent` product; in that order).

ctx_size.description: Context window of one slot of the server.

vram_peak_bytes.description: Highest used GPU memory (whole GPU) sampled during the request (1 Hz telemetry).

ram_peak_bytes.description: Highest used system RAM sampled during the request.

content_captured.description: The content of this request was captured (see `request_content`).

slots.description: Slots of the server that answered.

waited.description: `slots` / `tokens` when the request waited for its turn (see `RequestRecord::waited`).

tool_involved.description: The request offered tools, carried tool results or the response made a call.

tool_diag_category.description: Who is at fault: `runtime`, `context`, `model` or `client`; `None` for a clean round.

tool_diag_detail.description: Evidence as JSON text (tool name, excerpt, schema path, linked request...).

ResourceContent.description: One piece of a resource read (`resources/read` returns a list of them).

ResourceList.description: The resources and templates of one server.

store.description:
Store responses that ask for it (`store` is `true` unless the request says `false`).

continued) until retention drops them or they are cleared.

retention_days.description: Days a stored response is kept after it was created or last continued.

max_stored.description: Most stored responses kept (all callers together).

max_mib.description: Most bytes kept (JSON of input items and responses), MiB.

oneOf.description: Summarizing the older links of long chains.

RestartState.description: A scheduled automatic restart (shown as "restarting in N s, attempt k/N").

restart_at_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the restart begins.

option.description:
A recovery option id from `GET /servers/{id}/recovery` (its overrides and servers to
stop are used).

overrides.description: Catalog parameters over the last launch (added to the option's).

unload.description: Servers to stop first (added to the option's).

save.description: Also save the values to the model definition (and the profile's own overrides).

source.description: Where the router found it: `models_dir`, `preset` or `cache`.

path.description: The model file, when the router's arguments name one.

exit_code.description: Exit code of the last failed load.

wait_seconds.description:
Load only: wait up to this many seconds until the model is loaded (0 = answer at
once with the state the router reports).

RouterModelState.description: Load state of one model of a router.

workdir.description:
Working directory of file tools and the shell; default: `workdir` of the policy
settings. File tools cannot leave it.

approved.description: The caller asked the user and got a yes (see the module docs).

client.description: Client label for the tool log (default: the token's name, or `api`).

model.description: For the tool log: the model that wrote the call.

timeout_secs.description: Time limit in seconds (default 120, at most 600).

id.description: Id of the call in the tool log.

RuntimeAdvice.description: Runtime advice for a model (auto-suggestion from the GGUF tensor types).

special_types.description: Tensor types that not every build loads (empty = nothing to check).

official_unsupported.description: The official runtime can't load this file.

suggested_runtime.description: A registered runtime that loads every tensor type (preferring `current` when it does).

oneOf.description: The fork known to add these types, when no registered runtime loads them.

RuntimeDevice.description: A GPU device of the runtime.

index.description: Position in the runtime's list (the value `--main-gpu` takes; `--tensor-split` order).

free_bytes.description: Free memory as the runtime reports it.

os_used_bytes.description: Current usage of the matching OS adapter (all processes), when known.

available_bytes.description:
What a new model can use: the smaller of the runtime's free value and
`total - OS usage` (CUDA on Windows: `total - OS usage` alone, see `available_from`).

integrated.description: Integrated GPU (shares system memory); never part of a split suggestion.

family.description:
Runtime family (`llama.cpp`, later `whisper.cpp`); entries written before families
existed are llama.cpp.

files.description: Hashes of the executable files (checked at launch by size + mtime, fully by verify).

quant_types.description: Quant names its `llama-quantize --help` lists (empty = not detected).

missing.description: Tensor types this runtime can't load.

param_id.description: Catalog parameter that already covers this flag (set it there instead).

protected.description: Harness Studio manages this flag itself; it can't be added as a custom argument.

RuntimeFlag.description: A `--help` flag for the "all flags" explorer.

oneOf.description: A GitHub release archive (`owner/repo`, release tag, installed archives).

the folder is used in place (never modified or deleted by Harness).

RuntimeSummary.description: The llama-server binary the next start uses and what it can do.

Where the binary really comes from (`managed`, `custom`, `system` = found on PATH /
WinGet...); `None` when there is none.

fallback.description: The configured mode can't be used, `source` is a fallback.

binary_path.description: `None` when no llama-server is installed/configured (`error` says why).

name.description: Empty for the official runtime (the UI shows its own label).

oneOf.description: The registry entry (`None` for the official runtime).

available.description: The binary can be launched now (exists, files unchanged).

unsupported_params.description: Catalog parameters this binary has no flag for (hidden and never sent for it).

oneOf.description: Official runtime only: what Settings > Runtime is set to and what is really used.

Sampling parameters (llama-server `/completion` and `/v1/chat/completions` names).
`None` / empty = not sent (the server's or the model's default applies).

dynatemp_range.description: Dynamic temperature: temperature varies by +-range with the token entropy (0 = off).

adaptive_target.description: Adaptive-p: target probability of the picked token (negative / unset = off).

logit_bias.description: `{"<token id or text>": bias}` or llama-server's `[[token, bias]]` form.

json_schema.description: Constrain output to a JSON schema (llama-server `json_schema`).

headers.description:
Export headers, one `name=value` (or `name: value`) per line. Omitted/null = keep the
saved ones, `""` = remove them.

evidence.description: Log lines the classification is based on (at most 4).

The key requests to the server's own endpoint need: the user's, or the one made for this
run (a Python worker always has one). `null` when it needs none or is not running.

ServerRam.description: A running llama-server (with its child processes).

name.description: Model file name of the run.

Fulfil the hosted `web_search` tool a client asks for (Responses `web_search`, Chat

search provider the user configured (Settings > Tools).

tools.description:
Harness tools (registry names; MCP tools are `<server>_<tool>`) offered to the model on
every Chat / Responses / Messages request and run by the gateway. A tool the client
sends with the same name stays the client's.

max_sequence_tokens.description: Largest sequence length (prompt + generation) seen so far.

requests_observed.description:
Requests the poller saw complete (counters only move when a request finishes,
so requests finishing within the same second count once).

name.description: Profile name (instances without a profile: the id).

is_profile.description: A saved profile exists with this id.

served_alias.description: Model id the server serves (`/v1/models`): definition alias or file stem.

missing.description: File names of the missing parts.

response.description: Response as received (JSON, or the SSE event stream), cleaned.

Apple Silicon: memory the GPU may use (Metal `recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize`, estimated
from `hw.memsize` / `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` without Metal; see [`macos_gpu_budget`]).

intel_mac.description: Intel Mac (x86_64 macOS): no Metal build of llama.cpp; CPU only.

server_vram_used_bytes.description: This server's dedicated VRAM across adapters; None without a breakdown.

server_ram_used_bytes.description: This server's RAM share; None without a breakdown.

kv_usage_ratio.description: Share of the context window in use; None when the server exposes no such data.

predicted_tokens_per_sec.description: Current generation speed (from counter deltas over the last sample; 0 when idle).

prompt_tokens_per_sec.description: Current prompt processing speed (from counter deltas; 0 when idle).

kv_cache_usage_ratio.description: KV cache usage ratio, when the server still exposes it (older builds).

spec_acceptance_rate.description: Speculative decoding: accepted / drafted tokens (None when not drafting).

oneOf.description: Where the used system RAM goes; None until a system sample ran.

Where the used VRAM goes (same split as the RAM one, from per-process GPU memory
counters). None where the OS has no such counter for the GPU (macOS, NVIDIA on Linux)
or no sample ran: the view then shows an unsplit bar.

gpus.description:
Every graphics adapter with its own VRAM and split, in adapter order (the first is the
one `vram_*` above describe). Empty with a single adapter: the fields above are all.

context_size.description: Context window size and tokens held by busy slots (from /slots); None without slot data.

oneOf.description: Counters since the server started (None until /metrics answered).
Latest completed request seen by the poller.

TensorType.description: One tensor type of a model file.

TestExportResult.description: Result of "Test export": one real span sent to the configured endpoint.

trace_id.description: Trace id of the test span (search for it in the backend).

oneOf.description: Settings to test (may be unsaved); omitted = the saved ones.

headers.description: Headers to test with (unsaved); omitted = the saved ones.

allOf.description: Gateway policy: allowed models and endpoints, rate limits (empty = unrestricted).

TokenInfo.description: What lists and the API show about a named token.

TokenPolicy.description: The gateway policy of a named token (stored with it; see the module docs).

models.description: Model alias patterns (`*`, `?`); empty = every model.

endpoints.description: Gateway endpoint groups; empty = every endpoint.

TokenUpdate.description:
A change to a named token (`None` = keep). The secret never changes; to rotate it,
create a new token and revoke the old one.

oneOf.description: Replaces all three limits (a missing or `null` field = unlimited).

TokenizerInfo.description:
Tokenizer facts of a GGUF (`tokenizer.ggml.*`), enough to tell whether two models can
be target and draft of speculative decoding (see `library::draft`).

head_hash.description:
SHA-256 (hex, first 16 bytes) of the token texts from id [`TOKEN_HASH_START`]
([`TOKEN_HASH_LEN`] of them; llama.cpp compares token texts from id 5 on). `None` for
smaller vocabularies.

args.description: The arguments as JSON text, long strings shortened.

approved.description: The user approved this call when the policy asked.

ToolDef.description: A tool as the model and the clients see it.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema (`type: object`) of the arguments: the `parameters` of an OpenAI function.

uses_workspace.description: The tool works inside a working directory (file tools, shell).

decision.description: What a call would do under the current policy: run, ask or refuse.

server.description: The MCP server a tool comes from (`None` for built-in tools).

oneOf.description:
The class the tool has by itself (an MCP tool's annotation class), before the user's
own choice in `settings.tools.mcp_classes`; `def.class` is the one in force.

ToolEntry.description: A tool with what the current policy says about it.

ToolErrorCode.description:
Why a call did not produce a normal result. The text of the result says why in words (it
is what the model reads); the code is for programs.

ToolLimits.description: The limits as clients see them (`GET /tools`, the Playground's `tools_list`).

max_rounds.description: Tool rounds an agent loop runs before it stops and says so.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds one call may take (a tool may bound itself tighter).

max_result_chars.description: A result longer than this many characters is cut and the cut is marked.

ToolListing.description: `GET /tools`: the tools and the policy they are judged by.

mcp_expose.description: `settings.tools.mcp_expose`: the built-in tools are offered to MCP clients.

limits.description: Rounds, per-call time and result size every surface shares.

ToolResult.description: The result of one call, as the registry hands it back.

content.description: The text the model reads (the error sentence when `error` is set).

truncated.description: `content` was cut at the result size limit.

trusted.description: Tools the user trusts (names), honoured under "allow trusted".

workdir.description:
Working directory of file tools and the shell when the caller names none. Empty = none:
such calls fail with `no_workspace` instead of guessing.

workspaces.description:
Saved folders in most-recently-used order. None migrates legacy settings and
preserves the list when an older client saves only the original fields.

mcp_classes.description:
The user's permission class for an MCP tool (by its registry name, `<server>_<tool>`),
replacing the class its annotations give it. Only MCP tools: a built-in tool's class is
fixed in the code.

`None` = not given: saving settings from a screen that does not know the table keeps
the stored one (`save_settings`); `Some(empty)` clears it.

oneOf.description: Provider choice and non-secret endpoint for the provider-independent web_search tool.

mcp_expose.description:
Offer the built-in tools to MCP clients (`harness mcp`, `/mcp`) as well. Off by default
so existing clients do not suddenly see file and shell tools. The policy above still
decides each call; MCP cannot ask, so only calls the policy allows run.

undone.description:
`true` undoes the compaction (requests send the full history again), `false`
re-applies it.

alias.description: Stop every server serving this definition alias (or id).

Usage.description: Token counts and llama-server timings read from a response.

cached_tokens.description: Prompt tokens served from the KV cache (`timings.cache_n`, `cached_tokens`).

draft_n.description: Speculative decoding: drafted and accepted tokens.

VariantView.description: Settings > Runtime view: every build of this platform with its state.

download_bytes.description: Download size of the pinned archives (the real transfer is smaller for ZIPs).

damaged.description:
Files of an install that are missing or changed in size ([`damaged_in`]); the build then
reads as not installed and is installed again.

VerifiedCaps.description:
Chat-template capabilities as llama-server itself reported them (`/props`
`chat_template_caps`), recorded by the capability registry on every start.

reasoning.description:
The template takes a reasoning level (`supports_reasoning_effort`) or keeps the
reasoning of earlier turns (`supports_preserve_reasoning`). Reporting `false` is not
conclusive (templates that think but drop it from history report it too), so a
template-detected reasoning ability is not taken back.

template_reasoning.description:
The chat template the server really used (`/props.chat_template`) lets the model
reason: the fallback when the flags above stay `false` (hybrid Qwen3 reports neither,
yet its template switches thinking with `enable_thinking`). `None`: no template sent.

VerifyReport.description: Result of a full check of a runtime.

ok.description: Files match the recorded hashes and `llama-server --version` runs.

changed.description: Recorded files whose SHA-256 differs now.

added.description: Code files that weren't there when the runtime was added.

accepted.description: The new hashes were accepted (local runtimes, `accept_changes`).

accept_changes.description: Local runtimes: take the current files as the new baseline.

raw.description: First line of the `--version` output, verbatim.

version.description: `0.5.0-dev` on current builds; the build number on old ones (`version: 4589 (hash)`).

searxng_url.description: SearXNG base URL only. API keys are always held by the OS keychain.
